newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-CAMPESE LOOKS TO OVERSEAS FOR FINALE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-CAMPESE LOOKS TO OVERSEAS FOR FINALE.

text.p: Former Australia test winger David Campese said he is poised to play out his career in English or Italian club rugby, The Australian newspaper reported on Thursday.

The world record test try scorer, who retired from international rugby last December after 101 appearances for the Wallabies, may quit New South Wales before next season in favour of a move to Europe.
"I've got no idea what I'm doing next year," Campese, the scorer of 64 test tries, was quoted as saying. "I'm weighing up my options. England or Italy could be part of that."
Campese will miss the two-match series between New South Wales and Queensland, starting in Brisbane on Saturday, because of a niggling knee injury.
The 34-year-old veteran said he had not yet been made an offer to stay with New South Wales for their Super 12 campaign next year.
"I am disappointed to miss the interstate series like this and, yes, I might have already played my last game for New South Wales. But you can't worry about those sort of things," Campese said.
"I basically need three weeks off -- the knee has been troubling me for more than a month. I don't want to look bad because the knee is holding me back," he said.
Campese, who plays for Randwick in the Sydney club competition, has played in Italy for several seasons in the past during the northern hemisphere winter.
But his latest comments suggest his next move to Europe could be on a full-time basis.
